title: Embedded coefficients and the canonical constant quotient tower
statement: Let $\ell$ be prime, $E\subset\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ a finite subextension, $\pi\in\mathcal O_E$ a generator of its maximal ideal, and $X$ a Noetherian scheme. Use the embedded coefficients and local completeness predicates of [def-sfb-embedded-integral-model-coefficients]. On the coefficient-sized small pro-etale site $J$ of $X$ put $A=\operatorname{ULift}(\mathcal O_E)$ and $I=(\pi)A$. Let $R=A_J$, $B=\varprojlim_{n\geq0}(A/I^{n+1})_J$, $\varphi:R\to B$ the canonical scalar map, and $q_R,q_B$ their first quotient maps, as in [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence]. There exist equivalences $e_B$ from the ambient embedded continuous-coefficient derived category to $D(B)$ and $e_R$ from the ambient embedded constant-coefficient derived category to $D(R)$. They preserve and reflect local completeness for the respective first-reduction kernel ideals. Moreover $e_B\circ\operatorname{Res}_{\varphi}$ and $\operatorname{Res}_{\mathrm{embedded}}\circ e_R$, written in functor composition order, are naturally isomorphic. The equivalences are on all objects, without boundedness or completeness hypotheses.

Construct the exact section-action and AsSmall pushforward equivalences on modules, then their termwise derived equivalences. Identify the chosen-representative smallDerivedObject with these functor values.

proof.text: A commuting first-reduction square identifies the kernel ideals sectionwise by surjectivity of the scalar isomorphism and injectivity of the residue isomorphism. The local ideal condition and the existing restriction completeness theorem give preservation and reflection of completeness, after the canonical chosen-representative isomorphism.

proof.text: Restriction along each coefficient isomorphism gives the remaining exact module equivalence. Section-action commutes with scalar restriction, and AsSmall pushforward preserves the same sectionwise actions. Use the scalar square, associators and whiskering to compare the ordinary functors; derive this natural isomorphism using the composition isomorphisms.

lean.statement:
theorem embeddedIntegral_coefficient_presentation
    (ℓ : ℕ) [Fact ℓ.Prime] (E : PadicAlgCl.FiniteIntermediateField ℓ)
    (π : PadicAlgCl.integers ℓ E.1)
    (hπ : Ideal.span {π} = IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (PadicAlgCl.integers ℓ E.1))
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsNoetherian X] :
    let A := ULift.{u + 1} (PadicAlgCl.integers ℓ E.1)
    let I : Ideal A := Ideal.map ULift.ringEquiv.symm.toRingHom (Ideal.span {π})
    let J := Scheme.coefficientProEtaleModelTopology.{u, u} X
    ∃ (eB : DerivedCategory.{u + 1}
        (Mod (Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) Ab.{u + 1})
          (integralCoefficientObject X ℓ E)) ≌
        ConstantCompletion.D (ConstantCompletion.completed J A I))
      (eR : DerivedCategory.{u + 1}
        (Mod (Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) Ab.{u + 1})
          (condensedRingObj (IntegralModelsEmbedded.discreteObj
            (PadicAlgCl.integers ℓ E.1)) X)) ≌
        ConstantCompletion.D (ConstantCompletion.constant J A)),
      (∀ K, IntegralModelsEmbedded.completedComplete ℓ E π X K ↔
        ConstantCompletion.IsComplete (ConstantCompletion.projection J A I 0)
          (eB.functor.obj K)) ∧
      (∀ L, IntegralModelsEmbedded.constantComplete ℓ E π X L ↔
        ConstantCompletion.IsComplete (ConstantCompletion.quotient J A I 0)
          (eR.functor.obj L)) ∧
      Nonempty (eB.functor ⋙ ConstantCompletion.dres (ConstantCompletion.coefficientMap J A I) ≅
        IntegralModelsEmbedded.restriction ℓ E X ⋙ eR.functor)
